definitions.explanation: The physical size or scale of something. Formed from the adjective 大きい by replacing い with さ.

examples.japanese: この{箱|はこ}の{大|おお}きさはどのくらいですか。
りんごの{大|おお}きさがそれぞれ{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: The apples are each a different size.

examples.japanese: {靴|くつ}の{大|おお}きさが{合|あ}わなくて、{足|あし}が{痛|いた}い。
examples.english: The shoe size doesn't fit, so my feet hurt.

notes:
{大|おお}きさ means "size" or "magnitude" — the extent of how big something is.

FORMS:
Formed with the ～さ suffix that converts い-adjectives into nouns expressing degree:
- {大|おお}きい → {大|おお}きさ (size)
- {高|たか}い → {高|たか}さ (height)
- {長|なが}い → {長|なが}さ (length)
- {広|ひろ}い → {広|ひろ}さ (spaciousness)
- {小|ちい}さい → {小|ちい}ささ (smallness)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {大|おお}きさが{違|ちが}う: to differ in size
- {大|おお}きさが{同|おな}じ: to be the same size
- {大|おお}きさを{測|はか}る: to measure the size
- {大|おお}きさを{比|くら}べる: to compare sizes

USAGE:
Unlike English "size" which can also refer to clothing sizes (S/M/L), {大|おお}きさ primarily refers to physical dimensions. For clothing sizes, サイズ is more common: このサイズはありますか (Do you have this size?).
